# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 13
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "most sweet-smelling herbs" vs. "most fragrant herbs" vs. "herbs whose fragrance was overwhelming"
- **EMET:** "most sweet-smelling herbs"
- **LOGOS:** "most fragrant herbs"
- **PNEUMA:** "herbs whose fragrance was overwhelming"
- **Note:** "Overwhelming" (PNEUMA) adds an intensity not in source. "Fragrant" (LOGOS) is a natural upgrade of "sweet-smelling" (EMET).

### v.1 — "beautiful beyond anything I had words for" (PNEUMA addition)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "glorious and beautiful"
- **PNEUMA:** "glorious, beautiful beyond anything I had words for"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "beyond anything I had words for" is a narrative expansion not in source.

### v.3 — "the smell of the garden was surpassing" vs. "surpassed all things"
- **EMET:** "the smell of the garden was surpassing"
- **LOGOS:** "the fragrance of the garden surpassed all things"
- **PNEUMA:** "the fragrance — it surpassed everything"
- **Note:** LOGOS adds "all things" as an object for the comparative — a natural completion. PNEUMA's dash is a stylistic choice.

### v.5 — "in the garments of the angels of light" vs. "garments like the garments of the angels"
- **EMET:** "in the garments of the angels of light"
- **LOGOS:** "in garments like the garments of the angels of light"
- **PNEUMA:** "in garments like the garments of the angels of light — their clothing itself was made of light"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "made of light" addition is interpretive — the source says the clothing was *like* light, not *made of* light.

### v.7 — "brothers, the righteous" — all agree. No disagreement.

### v.8 — "shed their blood for you"
- All agents agree on this phrase. No disagreement.

### v.9 — "trees of healing"
- All agents retain. PNEUMA adds "trees of healing" more dramatically — no real disagreement on the phrase.

### v.12 — "gave all they had to the poor" vs. "gave everything they owned to the poor"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "gave all they had to the poor"
- **PNEUMA:** "gave everything they owned to the poor"
- **Note:** Minor. "All they had" vs. "everything they owned" — equivalent.

### v.12 — "feared not the torments of men" vs. "did not fear what men could do to them" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET:** "feared not the torments of men"
- **LOGOS:** "did not fear the torments of men"
- **PNEUMA:** "did not fear what men could do to them"
- **Note:** "What men could do to them" is a paraphrase; "torments of men" is more precise and preserves the martyrdom context.

### v.13 — "praising God with a joyful voice" — all agree.
- **PNEUMA** adds "full of joy" as a restatement — slight redundancy.

---
*10 disagreements. SOPHIA: "most fragrant herbs" (v.1); "like the light" not "made of light" (v.5); "torments of men" (v.12); preserve "surpassed all things" (v.3).*
